suggestions.rationale: Systematic-review and meta-analytic evidence shows higher prevalence and odds of depressive disorders and symptoms among people with alopecia areata. This supports focused mental-health review when a depressive disorder is diagnosed alongside alopecia areata, but the association alone does not establish an individual direction of effect or nexus without chronology, psychosocial-impact evidence, and assessment of other contributors.
evidenceGaps: Dermatology records establishing alopecia areata severity and chronology
Mental-health records establishing depressive-disorder diagnosis and chronology
Documentation of psychosocial, functional, body-image, or quality-of-life impact
Clinical assessment addressing other psychiatric, medical, medication, and psychosocial contributors

sourceReferences.citation: Lauron et al., Prevalence and Odds of Depressive and Anxiety Disorders and Symptoms in Children and Adults With Alopecia Areata: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis, JAMA Dermatol. 2023. PMID 36696123
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review/meta-analysis reporting elevated prevalence and odds of depressive and anxiety disorders and symptoms in alopecia areata; supports mental-health assessment rather than an automatic individual conclusion.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 36696123; abstract; separate analyses of depressive/anxiety disorders and symptoms in alopecia areata
